title: Chase Mobile Deposit Camera Black Screen on Android: Quick Fix Guide [2026]
content:
Using Chase [QuickDeposit](/guides/chase-quickdeposit-stuck-on-processing) on an Android device is supposed to be effortless: you tap deposit, align the check, and submit. However, if the camera viewfinder displays an **entirely black screen**, the app cannot capture check images.

This frustrating glitch is caused by Android camera hardware lockouts, missing OS permissions, or third-party camera overlays (like screen filters and blue-light dimmers).

## Why Is the Chase Camera Screen Black on Android?

**A black screen during mobile deposit occurs when Android's camera subsystem fails to release hardware access to the Chase app, or when runtime permissions have lapsed.** When two background processes compete for camera access, Android defaults to a black feed to prevent unauthorized access.

| Diagnostic Detail | Information |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Bank** | Chase Bank (QuickDeposit) |
| **Operating System** | Android (Samsung, Google Pixel, Motorola, OnePlus) |
| **Symptom** | Camera opens but displays black / blank rectangle |
| **Average Resolution Time** | 2 - 5 Minutes |

> 💡 **Quick Tip:** Ensure you have physical checks placed against a dark, non-reflective background with ample overhead lighting to prevent focus loop crashes once the camera feed restores.

## 6 Step-by-Step Solutions for Android Camera Black Screen

Follow these verified steps in sequential order to restore check deposit functionality:

### 1. Force Stop the Camera and Chase Apps
Android background camera sessions can become frozen in an active state:
1. Open your phone's **Settings**.
2. Go to **Apps** > **See all apps**.
3. Locate and tap **Camera**, then tap **Force Stop**.
4. Return to the app list, tap **Chase**, and tap **Force Stop**.
5. Relaunch Chase and navigate back to QuickDeposit.

### 2. Reset Chase Camera Permissions in Android Settings
Android privacy permissions occasionally desync after system security updates:
1. Go to **Settings** > **Apps** > **Chase**.
2. Tap **Permissions** > **Camera**.
3. Select **Don't allow**.
4. Wait 5 seconds, then tap **Allow only while using the app**.
5. Open Chase again. The app will re-initialize the camera driver.


> 💡 **Related Chase Bank Solution:** Encountering related issues? Check our verified fix for [Chase App Notifications Not Working on Android: Complete Push & 2FA Fix Guide](/guides/chase-app-notifications-not-working-android).



> 💡 **Related Chase Bank Solution:** Encountering related issues? Check our verified fix for [Chase App Not Working After Update: How to Fix App Store & Play Store Update Loops](/guides/chase-app-not-working-after-update).


### 3. Clear Chase App Cache and App Data
Stale cached camera preview buffers can corrupt the viewfinder:
1. Go to **Settings** > **Apps** > **Chase**.
2. Tap **Storage & cache**.
3. Tap **Clear Cache**.
4. If the black screen persists, tap **Clear Storage** (Clear Data).
*(Note: Clearing storage resets app preferences; you will need to re-enter your username and password).*

### 4. Disable Screen Overlays and Blue Light Filters
Third-party apps that draw over other apps (such as Twilight, blue-light filters, or screen recorders) trigger Android security flags that disable the camera:
1. Open **Settings** > **Apps** > **Special app access**.
2. Tap **Display over other apps**.
3. Temporarily turn off permissions for any screen tinting or recording apps.
4. Restart your device.

### 5. Check Hardware Access in Android Quick Settings
Modern Android releases (Android 12 and later) feature a global camera privacy toggle:
1. Swipe down twice from the top of your screen to open the **Quick Settings panel**.
2. Look for the tile labeled **Camera access**.
3. Ensure **Camera access** is toggled **ON** (green).
*If this toggle is off, all apps on your phone receive a blank black video feed.*

### 6. Restart Your Phone in Safe Mode (Isolate Third-Party Conflicts)
If another application is monopolizing camera hardware:
1. Press and hold your phone's **Power button**.
2. Touch and hold the **Power off** or **Restart** icon on screen until the **Safe Mode** prompt appears.
3. Tap **OK** to reboot into Safe Mode.
4. If the camera works in Safe Mode, a recently installed third-party app is the root cause. Uninstall suspect apps and restart normally.

## Prevention Tips

To ensure smooth mobile check deposits in the future:
* **Flatten the Check:** Ensure the check has no folded corners or creases before initiating the deposit.
* **Keep Camera Lens Clean:** Smudges on your camera lens prevent the automated autofocus algorithm from snapping the picture.
* **Maintain App Updates:** Keep the Chase app updated via the Google Play Store to receive camera compatibility patches.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Does a black camera screen mean my phone's camera hardware is broken?**
**No.** If your standard default Camera app can take pictures normally, your hardware is 100% intact. The issue is strictly an Android permission or software driver conflict with the Chase app.

**What is the maximum check amount I can deposit with Chase QuickDeposit?**
**Standard Chase consumer accounts generally feature a daily mobile deposit limit of $2,000 to $5,000, with a 30-day rolling limit of up to $10,000.** You can view your exact personalized limits on the deposit screen in the app.

**How long does it take for funds from a mobile deposit to clear?**
**Checks deposited before 11:00 PM Eastern Time on a business day are generally available the next business day.** Some funds may be released immediately based on your account history.

**What if I cannot get the camera to work and need the funds today?**
**You can deposit physical checks at any Chase ATM or branch teller.** ATM check deposits do not require an envelope and provide immediate printed receipts with check images.
